# Microsoft 365 Unified Audit Log Emission

The unified audit log (UAL) is the third emission plane and the one most often
assumed rather than verified. It covers Exchange Online, SharePoint, OneDrive,
Teams, Power Platform, and Purview activity — none of which appears in Entra
diagnostic settings or Azure activity logs.

## Step 1 — Verify auditing is actually on

Auditing is on by default for Microsoft 365 and Office 365 **enterprise**
organizations. It is **not** on by default for Small and Medium Business
licenses (Business Basic, Business Standard, Business Premium), and not for
unmanaged tenants using enterprise free trials
([turn auditing on or off](https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-enable-disable)).

```powershell
# Must be Exchange Online PowerShell.
Connect-ExchangeOnline
Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled
```

`True` means auditing is on.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Run this in Exchange Online PowerShell, not Security & Compliance PowerShell

`Get-AdminAuditLogConfig` exists in both modules. In Security & Compliance
PowerShell the `UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled` property is **always
`False`**, even when auditing is fully enabled
([turn auditing on or off](https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-enable-disable#before-you-turn-auditing-on-or-off)).

This produces a specific and expensive false negative: an operator confirms
"auditing is off," enables something that was already enabled, and — worse —
an assessor or an automated check records a finding against a compliant
tenant. Confirm which module the session is connected to before trusting the
output.
:::

## Step 2 — Enable if needed

Portal path: [Microsoft Purview portal](https://purview.microsoft.com) →
**Audit** solution card → select the **Start recording user and admin
activity** banner.

PowerShell:

```powershell
Connect-ExchangeOnline
Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true
```

Enabling takes up to **60 minutes** to take effect, and audit events may take
several more hours to become searchable. You need the **Audit Logs** role in
Exchange Online — held by default by the *Compliance Management* and
*Organization Management* role groups.

::: {.callout-important}
## Turning auditing off breaks everything downstream

With auditing disabled you cannot use the Office 365 Management Activity API
or Microsoft Sentinel to access audit data, Purview audit searches return no
results, and `Search-UnifiedAuditLog` returns nothing
([turn auditing on or off](https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-enable-disable)).

Changes to the auditing status are themselves audited. Include
`Set-AdminAuditLogConfig` in the SIEM's high-severity detection set — an
adversary disabling tenant auditing is a pre-exfiltration signal, and it is
one of the few events that destroys the evidence of everything that follows:

```powershell
Search-UnifiedAuditLog -Operations Set-AdminAuditLogConfig `
  -StartDate (Get-Date).AddDays(-90) -EndDate (Get-Date)
```
:::

## Step 3 — Register the app for API access

The Management Activity API is app-only. Register an application in Entra ID
in the **same national cloud as the tenant**, grant it Office 365 Management
APIs permissions, and admin-consent them.

| Setting | GCC (current boundary) | GCC High | DoD |
|---|---|---|---|
| API audience / resource | `https://manage-gcc.office.com` | `https://manage.office365.us` | `https://manage.protection.apps.mil` |
| Authority | `https://login.windows.net` | `https://login.microsoftonline.us` | `https://login.microsoftonline.us` |

Endpoint and authority values from the
[Management Activity API troubleshooting guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/office/office-365-management-api/troubleshooting-the-office-365-management-activity-api#troubleshooting-the-office-365-management-activity-api)
and the
[Office 365 Management API collection reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/guidance/coe/setup-auditlog-http#create-a-microsoft-entra-app-registration-for-office-365-management-api-access).
The commercial-cloud audience is `https://manage.office.com`.

::: {.callout-note}
## GCC differs here even though it matches worldwide elsewhere

Microsoft Graph and the Azure portal use worldwide endpoints for GCC. The
Management Activity API does **not** — GCC has its own `manage-gcc.office.com`
endpoint. This is the single most common cross-cloud misconfiguration on this
surface, because the Graph endpoint working reinforces the assumption that
everything else is worldwide too.
:::

## Step 4 — Subscribe to content types

Unlike Entra diagnostic settings, the Management Activity API has no
per-event-category selection. You subscribe per **content type**, and each
subscription is per tenant.

| Content type | Workload |
|---|---|
| `Audit.AzureActiveDirectory` | User sign-in and directory-change events as recorded by M365 |
| `Audit.Exchange` | Mailbox activity — reads, deletes, rule changes, admin actions |
| `Audit.SharePoint` | SharePoint and OneDrive file access, edits, sharing, downloads |
| `Audit.General` | All other workloads — Teams, Power Platform, Purview, Forms |
| `DLP.All` | Data Loss Prevention policy matches across all workloads |

Content types from the
[Management Activity API reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/office/office-365-management-api/office-365-management-activity-api-reference#working-with-the-office-365-management-activity-api).

Start a subscription:

```powershell
$tenantGUID = "<tenant-guid>"
$resource   = "https://manage-gcc.office.com"   # GCC; see the endpoint table

foreach ($contentType in @(
    'Audit.AzureActiveDirectory',
    'Audit.Exchange',
    'Audit.SharePoint',
    'Audit.General',
    'DLP.All'
)) {
    Invoke-WebRequest -Method Post -Headers $headerParams `
      -Uri "$resource/api/v1.0/$tenantGUID/activity/feed/subscriptions/start?contentType=$contentType"
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 900   # 15-minute throttle between start requests
}
```

Confirm what is actually subscribed:

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest -Method GET -Headers $headerParams `
  -Uri "$resource/api/v1.0/$tenantGUID/activity/feed/subscriptions/list"
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Two timing rules that break first-time integrations

**15-minute throttle.** After submitting a subscription-start request, a
15-minute wait is required before another can be made. Stopping a subscription
is not throttled.

**12-hour first blob.** "When a subscription is created, it can take up to 12
hours for the first content blobs to become available for that subscription."

Both from the
[Management Activity API reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/office/office-365-management-api/office-365-management-activity-api-reference#working-with-the-office-365-management-activity-api).
A team that subscribes all five content types in a loop and declares failure
an hour later has hit both rules at once — the loop was throttled and the data
was never due yet.
:::

## Step 5 — Retrieve content

Poll for available blobs, or register a webhook and be notified.

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest -Method GET -Headers $headerParams `
  -Uri "$resource/api/v1.0/$tenantGUID/activity/feed/subscriptions/content?contentType=Audit.AzureActiveDirectory&startTime=2026-08-26T00:00&endTime=2026-08-27T00:00"
```

Constraints from the
[API reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/office/office-365-management-api/office-365-management-activity-api-reference#list-available-content):

- `startTime` and `endTime` must both be supplied or both omitted.
- They must be no more than **24 hours** apart, with `startTime` no more than
  **7 days** in the past. Requests spanning more than 24 hours "could be
  partial results and should not be taken into account."
- Results paginate via a `NextPageUri` response header. Keep following it
  until a response arrives without one — a single page is not the full set.
- Set `PublisherIdentifier` to your organization's tenant GUID on every
  request to get a dedicated throttling quota. Requests without it share one
  global quota with every other caller who also omitted it.

::: {.callout-important}
## Events are not ordered, and this is by design

"The actions and events contained in the content blobs will not necessarily
appear in the order in which they occurred. One content blob can contain
actions and events that occurred prior to the actions and events contained in
an earlier content blob"
([API reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/office/office-365-management-api/office-365-management-activity-api-reference#working-with-the-office-365-management-activity-api)).

Any ingestion pipeline that assumes blob order equals event order, or that
uses "last blob retrieved" as a high-water mark, will silently drop events.
Track ingestion by `contentId`, deduplicate on it, and re-scan a trailing
window. This is a direct instance of the ADR-006 determinism requirement — no
silent drops — that the
[Telemetry Modernization Spec](../../modernization-specs/telemetry/telemetry.qmd)
imposes on every telemetry adapter.
:::

## Retention — the tier that decides the evidence

Enabling the UAL does not by itself satisfy AU-11 or OMB M-21-31. Retention is
governed by license tier and by audit retention policies:

| Tier | Retention |
|---|---|
| Audit (Standard) | **180 days** by default (logs generated before 2023-10-17: 90 days) |
| Audit (Premium) | **1 year** for Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, and `AzureActiveDirectory` workload records, via a non-modifiable default policy |
| Audit (Premium), all other workloads | **180 days** unless a custom retention policy extends them |
| Audit (Premium) + 10-year add-on | Up to **10 years**, per-user add-on license required |

From
[Manage audit log retention policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-retention-policies)
and
[auditing solutions in Microsoft Purview](https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-solutions-overview#audit-premium).

::: {.callout-warning}
## The default Premium policy is license-scoped, not tenant-scoped

The one-year default retention applies only to records for activity performed
by users assigned an Office 365 / Microsoft 365 **E5** license, a Microsoft
Purview Suite license, or the E5 eDiscovery and Audit add-on. "If you have
non-E5 users or guest users in your organization, their corresponding audit
records are retained for 180 days"
([audit log retention policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-retention-policies)).

Federal tenants are rarely uniformly E5. A mixed-license estate has a
**split retention horizon** that no dashboard displays: E5 users at one year,
everyone else — including every guest and every service account on a lower
SKU — at 180 days. Enumerate license assignment against the M-21-31 scope
before asserting a retention position, and record the mixed state explicitly
if it exists.

Retention policies are also **not retroactive**. A 10-year policy created
today cannot retain records generated yesterday.
:::

## Sentinel ingestion

For Sentinel, the **Microsoft 365** (Office 365) data connector ingests
Exchange, SharePoint, and Teams activity into the `OfficeActivity` table
without a custom Management API client. Use the connector for the
SOC-detection path and the Management Activity API for the substrate's
evidence path, where the
[SIEM adapter spec](../../adapter-specs/siem/siem.qmd) requires a
provenance envelope the connector does not produce.

Where both are running, they are independent readers of the same UAL. The
connector does not consume blobs in a way that hides them from an API
subscription.

## Verify emission

```kusto
// M365 unified audit emission health by workload.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| summarize Events = count(), LastEvent = max(TimeGenerated) by OfficeWorkload, RecordType
| extend Stale = LastEvent < ago(6h)
| order by Stale desc, Events desc
```

Tenant-side, independent of any SIEM:

```powershell
# Does the UAL itself hold recent records for each workload?
foreach ($wl in @('AzureActiveDirectory','Exchange','SharePoint','MicrosoftTeams')) {
    $n = (Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate (Get-Date).AddDays(-1) `
            -EndDate (Get-Date) -RecordType $wl -ResultSize 1).Count
    "{0,-22} {1}" -f $wl, $(if ($n -gt 0) { "OK" } else { "NO RECORDS" })
}
```

Run both. The KQL proves the SIEM is receiving; the PowerShell proves the
tenant is recording. A green KQL result with a stale pipeline can persist for
hours on cached data — only the tenant-side check distinguishes "nothing
happened" from "nothing is being captured."
